name: Shalby Ltd
title: Shalby Ltd - 540797 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Shalby Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 9.8% to INR318 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR46.4 crore and margin fell to 14.6% from 15.9%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 9.8% YoY to INR318 crore, while EBITDA was roughly flat at INR46.4 crore and PAT was unchanged at INR7.9 crore. Standalone (hospitals) performed better, with revenue up 9.1% to INR250 crore, EBITDA of INR45.7 crore and PAT up to INR23.5 crore. Management highlighted Gurugram (Shalby International) turning EBITDA positive for a second consecutive quarter, MedTech posting a fifth consecutive quarter of positive EBITDA, and net debt declining. Management said H2 will be stronger and reiterated double-digit top-line growth for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR44.8 crore; margin down from 19.5%
net debt reduced YoY per management
down 16% in H1; about 1,200 days a year earlier

segments.name: Hospitals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR250 crore (+9.1%), EBITDA INR45.7 crore with margin 18.2% (vs 19.5%), PAT INR23.5 crore. Growth led by nephrology/urology, oncology, general surgery and critical care alongside joint replacement.

segments.name: Shalby International (Gurugram)
segments.commentary: Revenue approx INR30 crore, up about 50% YoY; EBITDA positive for second consecutive quarter and H1 positive; cash breakeven targeted near exit of Q4 FY27 per management.

segments.name: MedTech (SMTL India + SAT Inc US)
segments.commentary: Consolidated revenue INR316 million; SMTL India INR224 million (+40%), SAT Inc INR286 million (+4%). Consolidated EBITDA INR3.6 million, fifth consecutive quarter of positive EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit top-line growth for FY27, citing H1 already near that level and confidence in H2.
EBITDA margin expected to improve vs prior year as all entities are now EBITDA positive; management expects benefits from operational efficiencies from Q3 FY27.

New MedTech supply chain expected to cut COGS, with P&L benefit from Q4 FY27 and full-quarter impact from Q1 FY28; management estimates implant manufacturing cost could fall a further 30-40% from current levels.
Expected NPPA price revision for implants in mid-November, described as overdue by about two years, to support revenue and EBITDA.
Gurugram unit expected to reach PBT-neutral with an additional 20-30% growth from current levels; cash breakeven expected near exit of Q3/Q4 FY27.
FY27 standalone ETR guided at about 45-50%; capex for H2 expected to be replacement-only, similar to H1's INR10 crore.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR10 crore, all replacement; H2 expected at similar levels with no significant growth capex, versus INR160 crore spent last year.
Gurugram (Shalby International) to add beds using additional FSI, expected operational in 12-18 months; technology investments include robotics, LINACs with bunkers, and a new PET-CT.
Mumbai expansion delayed significantly due to pending approvals with trustees; no update given.
Management said 80-90% of future internal accruals will go to hospitals rather than MedTech; MedTech expected to be self-sustaining with little new capital.
MedTech: reinstated in-house passivation line and recommissioned a secondary clean line in Clean, Pack & Sterile operations to add capacity.
demand_pricing: Standalone ARPOB up 4.3% to INR42,581; occupancy up 400 bps to 52% (55% ex-Gurugram); ALOS improved to 3.58 days.
Gurugram ARPOB up 18% to INR96,388; domestic business grew 56% and international about 22% YoY at the unit.

Onco price capping notification (about 180 molecules) expected effective mid-November; management said margin impact insignificant as company already near the government-expected ~30% margin from MRP, and most surgeries are packaged.
MedTech entered West Bengal and Odisha; reactivating Central India, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand next; approvals received in Malaysia, Argentina and Nepal, with more in progress.
Management said it is limiting FOSO (outsourced/franchise) operations to selected profitable ones; no aggressive expansion there.

qa_highlights.question: Why focus on hospitals rather than the implant subsidiary, which has weighed on consolidated PBT?
qa_highlights.answer: Shanay Shah said implant cost per unit fell from about $1,100 to less than half and could drop a further 30-40% with the new supply chain; management said MedTech will be self-sustaining with little new capital and 80-90% of new capital will go to hospitals.

qa_highlights.question: When will Gurugram contribute positively at PBT level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gurugram needs an additional 20-30% growth from current levels to reach PBT neutrality; cash breakeven is expected at the exit of Q3/Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of onco drug price capping?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said impact should be insignificant as margins are already close to the government's expected ~30% MRP margin, and surgeries are packaged so medicines are not sold separately.

qa_highlights.question: What expansion plans are there?
qa_highlights.answer: Gurugram bed addition using additional FSI in 12-18 months, technology upgrades (robotics, LINACs, new PET-CT); Mumbai expansion delayed pending trustee approvals with no update.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MedTech roadmap for the next 2-3 years on sales, EBITDA and debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers but said sales should rise significantly as margins improve, inventory days were cut from about 1,200 to around 784, and debt in implants should fall with fewer new product launches.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and tax rate expectations for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 capex about INR10 crore and H2 similar, replacement only; standalone tax rate 24% vs 35% last year, and ETR guided at about 45-50% from about 65% last year.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA flat YoY and margin down about 130 bps; consolidated PBT down about 14% YoY, so profit conversion remains weak.
Dependence on delivery of new MedTech supply chain (Q4 FY27 benefit) and inventory reduction; MedTech revenue remains small at INR316 million.
Timing of NPPA implant price revision (expected mid-November) and onco price capping implementation.
Gurugram unit still not PBT positive; success depends on 20-30% further growth and occupancy gains.
Mumbai expansion delayed by pending approvals; no timeline provided.
Rupee/dollar movement affected debt reduction per CFO; consolidated net debt about INR458 crore with gearing 0.45x.
Elevated ETR (45-50%) continues to weigh on net profit.
key_quotes: We believe H2 will be more exciting from here , and we look for a stronger year than the previous year.
So I'm unable to give you numbers because we are not kind of -- I mean, we have the projections with us, but we are not able to share it.
The Mumbai expansion, basically, we are working along with the trustees. It has been delayed quite significantly.

So what we believe is that the debt at the consolidated level will come down significantly because this time, you would have seen this is the first time in the last many quarters where we have seen a reduction in overall net debt.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on hospital growth, Gurugram progress, and the MedTech cost reset, and repeatedly said H2 would be stronger. It was cautious and vague on specifics: it declined to give MedTech sales or debt numbers, gave no timeline for Mumbai, and said expansion plans may not be worth disclosing yet.

adds.what: Gurugram (Shalby International) bed addition using additional FSI
MedTech recommissioned secondary clean line in Clean, Pack & Sterile operations and reinstated in-house passivation line

growth.why: Management reiterates double-digit FY27 revenue growth, with H1 near that level (Q2 revenue +9.8%), backed by ARPOB up 4.3%, occupancy up 400 bps to 52%, NPPA implant price revision and Gurugram growth of ~50%, but no major new capacity is funded since H1 capex was only about INR10 crore and Mumbai expansion is stalled.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects EBITDA margin to improve vs prior year from operational efficiencies from Q3 FY27 and MedTech COGS benefit from Q4 FY27, but Q2 consolidated margin fell to 14.6% from 15.9% and standalone margin to 18.2% from 19.5%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gurugram bed addition using additional FSI is expected operational in 12-18 months, but no capacity is funded at scale (H1 capex only about INR10 crore) and Mumbai expansion is delayed with no timeline.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterated double-digit FY27 top-line growth with Q2 consolidated revenue up 9.8% and standalone occupancy up 400 bps to 52%, plus Gurugram revenue up about 50% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: H1 capex was about INR10 crore versus INR160 crore last year, H2 guided to similar replacement-only levels, and 80-90% of future accruals are going to hospitals with no significant growth capex flagged.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated only double-digit FY27 revenue growth and did not raise guidance; Q2 revenue growth of 9.8% sits right at that threshold and PBT fell about 14% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consolidated PBT fell about 14% (INR19.1 crore to INR16.5 crore), EBITDA was flat, and FY27 ETR of 45-50% weighs on profit, while the MedTech and Gurugram benefits depend on Q4 FY27 timing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management mentioned technology investments (robotics, LINACs with bunkers, a new PET-CT) and new MedTech supply chain benefits, but gave no launch dates or revenue sizing.

rows.label: NPPA implant price revision (mid-November)
rows.why: Management described the revision as overdue by about two years and expects it to support revenue and EBITDA from mid-November 2026.

rows.label: MedTech implant cost reset via new supply chain
rows.why: Management says implant manufacturing cost could fall a further 30-40% from current levels, with P&L benefit from Q4 FY27 and full-quarter impact in Q1 FY28; MedTech inventory days already cut to 784 from about 1,200.

rows.label: Gurugram PBT neutral and cash breakeven
rows.why: Gurugram revenue is about INR30 crore (+50% YoY) with ARPOB up 18% to INR96,388; management needs a further 20-30% growth to be PBT neutral and expects cash breakeven near exit of Q4 FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on hospital growth, Gurugram turnaround and the MedTech cost reset, but vague on MedTech sales/debt numbers and gave no Mumbai timeline; analysts pressed on weak PBT conversion and why Gurugram and MedTech still do not contribute at PBT level.
